{{Short description|Mathematical series, portmanteau of "Fibonacci" and "factorial"}}
{{More sources needed|date=May 2024}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Fibonorial''' {{math|''n''!<sub>''F''</sub>}}, also called the '''Fibonacci factorial''', where {{math|''n''}} is a [[nonnegative integer]], is defined as the product of the first {{math|''n''}} positive [[Fibonacci numbers]], i.e.

: <math>{n!}_F := \prod_{i=1}^n F_i,\quad n \ge 0,</math>

where {{math|''F''<sub>''i''</sub>}} is the {{math|''i''}}<sup>th</sup> Fibonacci number, and {{math|0!<sub>''F''</sub>}} gives the [[empty product]] (defined as the [[multiplicative identity]], i.e. 1).

The Fibonorial {{math|''n''!<sub>''F''</sub>}} is defined analogously to the [[factorial]] {{math|''n''!}}. The Fibonorial numbers are used in the definition of [[Fibonomial coefficient]]s (or Fibonacci-binomial coefficients) similarly as the factorial numbers are used in the definition of [[binomial coefficients]].

== Asymptotic behaviour ==

The [[Series (mathematics)|series]] of fibonorials is [[Asymptote|asymptotic]] to a function of the golden ratio <math>\varphi</math>: <math>n!_F \sim C \frac {\varphi^{n (n+1)/2}} {5^{n/2}}</math>. 

Here the ''fibonorial constant'' (also called the ''fibonacci factorial constant''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mathworld.wolfram.com/FibonacciFactorialConstant.html|title=Fibonacci Factorial Constant|last=W.|first=Weisstein, Eric|website=mathworld.wolfram.com|language=en|access-date=2018-10-25}}</ref>)  <math>C</math> is defined by <math>C = \prod_{k=1}^\infty (1-a^k)</math>, where <math>a=-\frac{1}{\varphi^2}</math> and <math>\varphi</math> is the [[golden ratio]].

An approximate truncated value of <math>C</math> is 1.226742010720 (see {{OEIS|id=A062073}} for more digits).

== Almost-Fibonorial numbers ==

Almost-Fibonorial numbers: {{math|''n''!<sub>''F''</sub> &minus; 1}}.

Almost-Fibonorial primes: [[prime numbers]] among the almost-Fibonorial numbers.

== Quasi-Fibonorial numbers ==

Quasi-Fibonorial numbers: {{math|''n''!<sub>''F''</sub> + 1}}.

Quasi-Fibonorial primes: [[prime numbers]] among the quasi-Fibonorial numbers.

== Connection with the q-Factorial ==

The fibonorial can be expressed in terms of the [[q-factorial]] and the [[golden ratio]] <math>\varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}2</math>:
:<math>n!_F = \varphi^{\binom n 2} \, [n]_{-\varphi^{-2}}!.</math>

== Sequences ==

{{OEIS2C|A003266}} Product of first {{math|''n''}} nonzero Fibonacci numbers {{math|''F''(1), ..., ''F''(''n'')}}.

{{OEIS2C|A059709}} and {{OEIS2C|A053408}} for {{math|''n''}} such that {{math|''n''!<sub>''F''</sub> &minus; 1}} and {{math|''n''!<sub>''F''</sub> + 1}} are primes, respectively.
